tasks.title: How many customers
tasks.statement: How many customers are in the customers table? Output the number as n (COUNT(*)).

tasks.title: How many products
tasks.statement: How many products are in products?

tasks.title: How many orders
tasks.statement: How many orders are in the orders table? Column n.

tasks.title: Only with a city
tasks.statement: How many customers gave a city (COUNT(city))? COUNT(column) skips NULL. Column n.

tasks.title: Distinct cities
tasks.statement: How many distinct cities do customers have (COUNT(DISTINCT city))? Column n.

tasks.title: Distinct categories
tasks.statement: How many distinct product categories are there? Column n.

tasks.title: Customers with orders
tasks.statement: How many distinct customers placed at least one order? COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) over orders. Column n.

tasks.title: Total stock
tasks.statement: How many units of goods are in stock in total? SUM(stock) as total_stock.

tasks.title: Total of all orders
tasks.statement: What is the total amount of all orders? SUM(total) as revenue.

tasks.title: Average
tasks.statement: What is the average product price? Output ROUND(AVG(price), 2) as avg_price.
tasks.hint: AVG returns a fractional number; ROUND(x, 2) rounds to hundredths.

tasks.title: Minimum and maximum
tasks.statement: Output the lowest and the highest price: min_price and max_price.

tasks.title: Price spread
tasks.statement: Output the difference between the highest and the lowest price as spread.

tasks.title: MIN/MAX for dates
tasks.statement: Output the earliest and the latest order date: first_order, last_order.
tasks.hint: MIN and MAX work with both strings and dates.

tasks.title: MIN/MAX for text
tasks.statement: Output the smallest and the largest (alphabetically) customer name: first_name, last_name.

tasks.title: Aggregate and WHERE
tasks.statement: How many orders have the status 'paid'? Column n.

tasks.title: Revenue of paid orders
tasks.statement: What is the sum of orders with the status 'paid'? Column revenue.

tasks.title: Average check
tasks.statement: The average order amount among paid and shipped orders (status IN ('paid','shipped')), rounded to an integer: avg_check.

tasks.title: Most expensive in a category
tasks.statement: What is the highest price among products of the category `Электроника`? Column max_price.

tasks.title: How many units sold
tasks.statement: How many units of goods were sold in total according to the order_items table (SUM(qty))? Column sold.

tasks.title: Revenue by order lines
tasks.statement: What is the sum of qty * price over all order_items lines? Column amount.
tasks.hint: An aggregate can be computed over an expression.

tasks.title: Lines of a product
tasks.statement: How many order lines contain the product with id = 3? Column n.

tasks.title: Units of a product sold
tasks.statement: How many units of the product with id = 3 were sold in total? Column sold.

tasks.title: Aggregate over an empty selection
tasks.statement: SUM over an empty set is NULL. Output SUM(total) for orders with the status 'refund' (there are none) as s and COUNT(*) as n.

tasks.title: COALESCE around SUM
tasks.statement: Do the same, but output 0 instead of NULL: COALESCE(SUM(total), 0) as s.

tasks.title: TOTAL
tasks.statement: The total() function always returns a number (0.0 for an empty set). Output total(total) for the status 'refund' as t.

tasks.title: AVG and NULL
tasks.statement: AVG ignores NULL. Output AVG(rating) over the movies and COUNT(rating) as cnt (not every movie has a rating), rounding the mean to 2 decimals: avg_rating, cnt.

tasks.title: Glue values
tasks.statement: The group_concat function collects values into a string. Output the category names (without duplicates) separated by commas: SELECT group_concat(DISTINCT category) AS cats.

tasks.title: Glue with a separator
tasks.statement: Output the names of customers from `Тверь` joined with ' | ' (in id order): group_concat(name, ' | ') as names. Hint: first a subquery with ORDER BY id.

tasks.title: Share
tasks.statement: What share (in percent, ROUND to an integer) do VIP customers make up? 100.0 * SUM(vip) / COUNT(*) as vip_pct.
tasks.hint: vip stores 0 or 1, so SUM(vip) is the number of VIPs.

tasks.title: Conditional count
tasks.statement: In a single row output the number of orders by status: paid_n, new_n, cancelled_n — via SUM(status = '...').

tasks.title: Expensive products
tasks.statement: How many products cost more than the average price? Hint: the subquery (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products). Column n.

tasks.title: All aggregates at once
tasks.statement: In a single row over the products table: cnt (count), total_price (sum of prices), min_price, max_price, avg_price (rounded to an integer).

tasks.title: HR: payroll
tasks.statement: HR database. Output the sum of salaries as payroll and the average (ROUND to an integer) as avg_salary.

tasks.title: HR: highest salary
tasks.statement: HR database. Output the largest and the smallest salary: max_salary, min_salary.

tasks.title: HR: how many without a department
tasks.statement: HR database. How many employees have a department (COUNT(dept_id)) and how many in total (COUNT(*))? with_dept, total.

tasks.title: HR: newcomers
tasks.statement: HR database. How many employees were hired after 2023-01-01? n.

tasks.title: School: average grade
tasks.statement: School database. The average grade for 2024 (ROUND to 2 decimals): avg_score. NULL grades are ignored.

tasks.title: School: how many fives
tasks.statement: School database. How many fives (top grades) were given over all years? n.

tasks.title: School: total hours
tasks.statement: School database. The total number of hours across all courses: SUM(hours) as total_hours.

tasks.title: Movies: budget
tasks.statement: Movies database. How many movies have a known budget (cnt) and what is the total budget (total_budget)?

tasks.title: Movies: best rating
tasks.statement: Movies database. Output the highest rating as best.
